shouldFix.title: actor-join v8 defines each of the thirteen classes in 32 to 577 characters and the catalog carries none of those definitions, so a class reduces to a bare identifier
shouldFix.finding: The catalog pins actor-join v8 at a digest that reproduces and calls it the 'Source of the thirteen class names'. It is more than that. v8's joinFixtureClasses.classes are not bare ids: each entry is an id followed by an em dash and a definition. FC-JOIN-PERMISSIONREF-RESERVED gets 32 characters — 'populating permissionRef refuses'. FC-JOIN-COMPONENT-TAIL gets 577, on how every subsequent effect of an admitted child stays in DR-105 after a host CA-1 SPAWN decision. FC-JOIN-CA2-D000-GATE gets 227, on CA-2 remaining denied even when FC-C1 and DR-119 are present. I extracted all thirteen and measured each. The catalog's namedClasses entries carry exactly two fields, id and bytes, and I tested every definition for presence in the artifact: zero of thirteen are carried. The consequence is that a class in this catalog is an identifier and nothing else. A fixture author handed FC-JOIN-COMPONENT-TAIL cannot build it from what is here; they must leave for v8, which is the artifact this catalog exists to carry forward. It also means the catalog contributes nothing its own cited sources do not already hold, while losing what they do hold — leftover-join v2 already carries the same thirteen ids in the same order, and v8 carries them with their definitions.
shouldFix.whyItMatters: Every sibling in this catalog family carries the source's per-class content and that is what makes them useful: FC-REDACT carries all ten of v4's pass-property fragments, one per state; FC-NC carries both pass limbs; FC-SCHEMA carries all five outcome-class names character-exact. This one carries thirteen ids. The pattern the family establishes is that a catalog turns a source's prose into an enumerated, checkable set with the source content attached; here only the enumeration survives, and it was already enumerated.
shouldFix.whyNotABlocker: The artifact misstates nothing and overclaims nothing. It says it names identities and it names them, correctly and in order, against two sources. The definitions are one hop away in an artifact it pins by digest, and its purpose is honestly scoped to naming. That is the same mitigation structure that kept the FC-NC and FC-HOSTILE findings at SHOULD-FIX rather than blocker.
shouldFix.whatWouldRepairIt: Carry each class's v8 definition verbatim on its namedClasses entry — a definitionVerbatim field beside id and bytes, with the source path named as the sibling catalogs do. Thirteen strings, all already written, all in a pinned artifact.

advisories.title: No failsIf and no whatThisCloses block
advisories.detail: The artifact exposes none of its own claims to refutation and carries no closure block stating what would and would not be closed if it were accepted and recorded. It does better than the harness-specification siblings on the related point — it names OBL-JOIN-FX-AUTHORING explicitly in purpose and doesNot, so a recording act has an identifier to attach to — but a reader still cannot see, in one place, that acceptance would close nothing by itself and that FC-C1, the BLK-1..4 discharges and the thirteen implementations all remain.

advisories.title: namedGate 'none' is terser than the standing it reproduces
advisories.detail: The subject sets namedGate to 'none'. leftover-join v2's own field is existingGate 'none as authored implementations', which says something narrower and more useful: there is no gate for these as AUTHORED IMPLEMENTATIONS, which is why the remainder is execution-only and not capable of riding. The subject's rideStanding does carry the full phrase, so the standing is recoverable from the artifact; the bare 'none' in the more prominent field is the looser of the two.

Five of five cited digests reproduce. This Claude 2 write path was free, so unlike the five sibling doctor-fc catalogs dispatched immediately before it, this verdict is filed rather than reported only in chat. Every test the dispatch names is refuted, and the central one is refuted twice: the thirteen class ids are ORDERED-EQUAL to leftover-join v2's OBL-JOIN-FX-AUTHORING array and all thirteen also occur in actor-join v8, so neither source holds an id the catalog lacks nor the reverse. rideStanding reproduces v2's 'not-capable-of-riding as execution-only remainder' exactly. The G09 non-ride is verified against DR-G09's own live claim cell — permission truth, not join-fixture execution — rather than asserted, and G09 v3's ACCEPT 0/0 standing verifies against its own verdict file. No gate invented, no DR-G* row, no FC-C1 recording, no bytes: all thirteen classes carry NOT-AUTHORED, and the artifact's only four 64-hex strings are its own citations. It also names the obligation it continues, which the harness-specification siblings do not. The finding is content the catalog drops. actor-join v8's joinFixtureClasses are not bare ids — each is an id, an em dash, and a definition running from 32 characters for FC-JOIN-PERMISSIONREF-RESERVED to 577 for FC-JOIN-COMPONENT-TAIL. I extracted all thirteen and tested each for presence: zero are carried. A class here is therefore an identifier and nothing else, and a fixture author handed FC-JOIN-COMPONENT-TAIL cannot build it from what is on the page. It also leaves the catalog contributing nothing its own cited sources do not already hold while losing what they do — v2 already carries the same ids in the same order, v8 carries them with their meanings. Not a blocker: nothing is misstated, the purpose is honestly scoped to naming, and the definitions sit one hop away in a pinned artifact — the same mitigation that kept the FC-NC and FC-HOSTILE findings at SHOULD-FIX. The repair is thirteen verbatim strings that already exist.
